cohort: Women with prolonged preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) at 34(+0) -36(+6) weeks of gestation and detection of vaginal or urine group B streptococcus (GBS)
finding: For women with PPROM and GBS at 34-36 weeks gestation, immediate birth is more cost-effective than expectant management, resulting in higher QALYs and lower lifetime costs.
